newsitem.title: USA: First Union to buy Signet for $3.25 billion.
newsitem.headline: First Union to buy Signet for $3.25 billion.

text.p: First Union Corp. said Monday it will acquire Signet Banking Corp. in a $3.25 billion stock transaction that will create a banking powerhouse in and around the nation's capital.

First Union, the nation's sixth-largest bank, said the combined company, which will keep the First Union name, will have about $155 billion in assets and 2.2 million customers in Virginia, Maryland and the District of Columbia.
The company, which is based in Charlotte, N.C., said it expected to take an after-tax charge of $135 million this year to cover costs related to the merger.

In addition to ranking first in market share in Virginia, the combined company will rank second in market share in the Virginia, Maryland and Washington D.C. region, where First Union is currently the fourth-largest banking company, with deposits of $11.7 billion and assets of $16.8 billion.
First Union, which has 3,795 employees, 210 branches and 299 ATMs in the region, will acquire Signet's 4,000 employees, 230 branches and 248 ATMs. Signet is based in Richmond, Va.

"This is a financially driven combination that will give First Union a leading position in very attractive markets," said Edward E. Crutchfield, chairman and chief executive of First Union, a bank holding company with offices in 12 states, from Connecticut to Florida.

"The strong presence Signet has established in Richmond, Baltimore and Hampton Roads is a perfect fit for First Union's leading presence in Roanoke and our strong market position in Washington, D.C.," Crutchfield said.

First Union will exchange 0.55 share of its common stock for each share of Signet, valuing Signet at about $53.59 a share. Reflecting First Union's previously announced two-for-one stock split payable July 31, the exchange ratio will be 1.10 First Union shares for each Signet share.
The companies expect the merger, which will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, to close by Dec. 31, pending Signet shareholder approval, regulatory approval and other customary conditions.
First Union said it expects the merger will have a positive impact on earnings starting next year.

First Union said these expectations are based on estimated savings of 50 percent of Signet's annual expenses, or $242 million, as well as incremental revenue growth of $37 million as First Union brings its financial products and services to Signet customers.
The conversion of Signet's operating systems is expected to take about four months.
Following the merger, Signet Chairman and Chief Executive Malcolm McDonald will become CEO of First Union's Virginia, Maryland and Washington region.
Benjamin Jenkins III, current president of First Union's operations in the region, will become chief operating officer.
In connection with the merger agreement, Signet granted First Union an option to buy, under certain circumstances, up to 19.9 percent of Signet's outstanding common stock.
After the merger, First Union will rescind its existing authorisation to buy back stock, which authorised the repurchase of up to 25 million shares (or 50 million, adjusted for the stock split).
So far this year First Union has repurchased about 11 million shares under the authorisation, or about 22 million on a post-split basis.
